tagline: A goldfields city that holds the story of Australia's only armed rebellion
description: Ballarat is Victoria's third-largest city, about 110 km north-west of Melbourne. Gold found at Poverty Point on 18 August 1851 turned a sheep station into a major settlement within months. Sovereign Hill, a 25-hectare open-air museum, recreates the town's first ten years, and the Eureka Flag from the 1854 stockade rebellion is held in the city. The Botanical Gardens date from 1857, and Lake Wendouree hosted the 1956 Olympic rowing and kayaking.
whyVisit: Stroll the botanical gardens and lake

goodToKnow.title: Trams run weekends only
goodToKnow.detail: The Ballarat Tramway Museum runs historic trams beside Lake Wendouree on weekends and public and school holidays, from about 12:30 to 5pm.

goodToKnow.title: Plan transport between sights
goodToKnow.detail: Ballarat is a day trip from Melbourne by train or car, but the big sights are spread out, so work out how you will get between them.

goodToKnow.title: Book for Begonia Festival
goodToKnow.detail: The Begonia Festival over the March Labour Day weekend fills Lake Wendouree and Sturt Street, so book accommodation ahead.

bestTimeBlurb: Come in {months} for cooler air than Melbourne, plus the Begonia Festival in March.
notes: No source states best months; inferred from Ballarat's cooler elevated climate and the March festival.

tagline: A gold-rush boomtown of Victorian hotels, mine diggings and a lively arts scene
description: Castlemaine is a goldfields town founded in 1851, about 123 km from Melbourne and 39 km from Bendigo. Grand gold-era buildings and Victorian hotels survive on most street corners, and mullock heaps and mine shafts mark the Castlemaine Diggings National Heritage Park. Its Theatre Royal, established in 1854, is the oldest continuously operating theatre in mainland Australia. Maldon, 19 km away, was declared Australia's first notable town in 1966 for its largely unchanged 1850s buildings.
whyVisit: See a show in a historic theatre

goodToKnow.title: Steam train to Maldon
goodToKnow.detail: The Victorian Goldfields Railway runs from Castlemaine station to Maldon mostly Fridays to Sundays, so plan a weekend visit around it.

goodToKnow.title: Stay on marked tracks
goodToKnow.detail: Open mine shafts and mullock heaps lie off the goldfields trails, so keep to signed paths when bushwalking.

bestTimeBlurb: Walk the diggings and Maldon's streets in {months}, when inland weather is mild.
notes: Best months are a judgement from inland Victoria climate; no source states them.

tagline: A port city on Corio Bay and the gateway to the Bellarine and Great Ocean Road
description: Geelong is Victoria's second-largest city, home to 282,809 people in 2023, on Corio Bay about 75 km south-west of Melbourne. Its waterfront is a working maritime area with cafes, an antique carousel and botanical gardens. The National Wool Museum on Moorabool Street takes about 90 minutes and holds a tourist information office. You Yangs Regional Park, 22 km north, has a 3.2 km walk to Flinders Peak (348 m).
whyVisit: Walk up to wide hill views

goodToKnow.title: Avalon Airport is close
goodToKnow.detail: Avalon Airport, a second Melbourne-area airport, is about 20 minutes by road from Geelong, with a shuttle to Geelong and South Geelong stations.

goodToKnow.title: Cycle to Queenscliff
goodToKnow.detail: The 35 km Bellarine Rail Trail starts near South Geelong Station and runs to Queenscliff.

bestTimeBlurb: Holidaymakers flock to the beaches in {months}, with summer weekends the busiest.
notes: Best months inferred from summer beach holiday traffic; no source states them.

tagline: A Great Ocean Road coastal town beside Cape Otway and the Otway rainforest
description: Apollo Bay is a coastal town of 1,790 people on the Great Ocean Road, about 191 km from Melbourne. Cape Otway Lightstation, about 30 minutes away, has operated since 1848 and is the oldest surviving lighthouse on mainland Australia. In the hills behind, Maits Rest is a 30-minute rainforest boardwalk with glow worms at night, and the Otway Fly is a steel canopy walk 600 m long and up to 47 m high. The 104 km Great Ocean Walk passes through town on its way to the Twelve Apostles.
whyVisit: Watch southern right whales from shore

goodToKnow.title: Colac route is faster
goodToKnow.detail: Driving via Colac is much quicker than the Great Ocean Road, so use the coast road when you have time for the scenery.

goodToKnow.title: Book Great Ocean Walk camps
goodToKnow.detail: The walk's designated campsites have limited numbers and must be booked beforehand.

goodToKnow.title: Check falls track access
goodToKnow.detail: Parks Victoria closed the walking track to Marriner's Falls in 2011 over falling-tree risk, so check access before driving out.

bestTimeBlurb: Walk the coast in {months}, or come in winter and spring to see southern right whales.
notes: Warm-month choice is judgement. Whale season is winter to spring, exact months unsourced, so left out of seasonalTags. The Marriner's Falls closure dates from 2011 and may be stale; verify.

tagline: Victoria's largest national park, with its highest peak and the Bogong High Plains
description: Alpine National Park covers 6,474 km2 and is the Victorian continuation of Kosciuszko National Park. It holds Victoria's highest point, Mount Bogong at 1,986 m, along with Mount Feathertop (1,922 m), Mount Hotham (1,862 m) and the sub-alpine woodland and grassland of the Bogong High Plains. The 650 km Australian Alps Walking Track, from Walhalla to near Canberra, crosses it. The park protects threatened species including the spotted tree frog, smoky mouse and mountain pygmy possum.
whyVisit: Hike the Australian Alps Walking Track

goodToKnow.title: Winter means skis
goodToKnow.detail: In winter much of the park is snow-covered and only accessible on skis.

goodToKnow.title: No towns inside
goodToKnow.detail: There are no towns in the park. Stay at Mount Hotham or Falls Creek, or in the towns around it.

goodToKnow.title: Unsealed road to falls
goodToKnow.detail: The road to Paradise Falls needs 11 km of unsealed driving. Spring or early summer is the best time to see it.

bestTimeBlurb: Walk and ride in {months}, when the alpine air is cool. Winter snow means skis.
notes: Summer months from the park's reputation for bushwalking and mountain biking. Ski season (roughly June to September) has unsourced months, so no seasonalTags. Wildflowers were in the researcher's experiences but not in a sourced fact, so the fourth reason uses the sourced Paradise Falls.

tagline: A north-east Victorian city at the gateway to Ned Kelly country and wine valleys
description: Wangaratta is a city of 29,808 people at the junction of the Ovens and King rivers, 236 km from Melbourne on the Hume Freeway. Glenrowan, 14 km away, is where bushranger Ned Kelly made his last stand in 1880, and its vines were first planted in 1866. In the King Valley, Italian migrants of the 1940s and 1950s switched from tobacco to wine, and the valley is known for sangiovese, nebbiolo and barbera. The 95 km Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail starts here.
whyVisit: Taste Italian varieties in wine valleys

goodToKnow.title: Warby Ranges get hot
goodToKnow.detail: Bushwalking in Warby-Ovens National Park can be very hot in summer, so walk in the cooler months or early in the day.

goodToKnow.title: Ride the rail trail
goodToKnow.detail: The Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail is sealed for almost its whole 95 km, so ordinary bikes cope.

bestTimeBlurb: Come in {months} to avoid the summer heat that makes Warby Ranges walks tough.
notes: Only two experiences were sourced, matching the rank 5 count. Months follow the sourced summer-heat caution.

tagline: A Murray River port where paddle steamers still sail from the historic wharf
description: Echuca sits on the Murray River, with the New South Wales town of Moama opposite, and has 15,056 people. Its port is home to the largest paddle steamer fleet in the world, including PS Adelaide (1866), the world's oldest operating wooden-hulled paddle steamer. PS Pevensey (1911) and PS Alexander Arbuthnot (1923) sail commercially from the port daily. Echuca is about 2.5 hours' drive from Melbourne.
whyVisit: Cruise the Murray on a paddle steamer

goodToKnow.title: Sit in the front carriages
goodToKnow.detail: On the train from Melbourne, sit in the front 3 cars, as the rear 3 decouple at Bendigo.

goodToKnow.title: Easy to walk around
goodToKnow.detail: Apart from occasional buses there is no town transport, but the town is small enough to walk.

goodToKnow.title: Southern 80 in February
goodToKnow.detail: February brings the Southern 80 waterski race and a music festival, so expect busy river banks and book ahead.

bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months} for river cruises without the February Southern 80 crowds.
notes: Sources give no best-time guidance; spring and autumn inferred. The Barmah forest reason is generalised from the researcher's experiences list.
